name: transition/curtain-reveal
title: Curtain Reveal
desc_vi: Hai tấm màn nhung đóng lại rồi vén ra hai bên, các nếp co mạnh nhất ở mép ngoài, lộ cảnh mới; đèn rọi ấm sáng lên khi màn mở.
params_vi: duration (1.7 s = cover 0.3 + vén 1.1 + out 0.3) · cover: màn hiện ra · out: màn mờ đi · tone: red | burgundy | navy | forest · pelmet · spotlight
notes: Added for a scene change (the source starts with the curtains already closed and keeps them bunched at the sides): the curtains and pelmet fade in over `cover` s (default 0.3) on top of the outgoing scene, the incoming scene appears behind them at the end of that fade, and curtains plus spotlight fade out over the last `out` s (default 0.3). The draw itself is the source's: 11 folds per curtain from the fixed width tables, power2.inOut over 1.1 s, fold scale sx = 1 - p(0.86 - 0.16u), sy = 1 - 0.07 p u^2, shade 0.34(1 - sx), scalloped pelmet, spotlight 0 -> 0.9 from 0.25 x draw over 0.75 x draw. Every fold pose is linear in the eased progress, so each fold is one literal tween (x, scaleX, scaleY) plus one shade tween; the shade (::after, black at opacity 0.34(1 - sx) in the source) is a real child box whose background colour rgba(0,0,0,a) is tweened (same look; an opacity layer on 22 transformed folds made the renderer's pixels differ between seeks). The source stage slot is the incoming scene. ae is png because of the layered gradients, box-shadows, clip-path hem and screen-blend spotlight. will-change: transform, opacity is set on the curtain group so the renderer gives the same pixels after a seek (many transformed gradient folds are otherwise slightly noisy).
